error_handling.overview: Reviewing can fail as easily as coding. These are the common failures and the correct response. In every case: say what happened, say what it means for the verdict, and lower the confidence.

scenario.name: build_fails

response.step: Report the first error only, with file and line.
State that no runtime finding is proven, because nothing ran.
Set the verdict to "Do not ship" and stop the deeper passes.

scenario.rule: Do not review logic you cannot compile. Read for clarity at most, and label it as inference.

scenario.name: tests_fail_for_unrelated_reasons
scenario.trigger: The test run fails in code the change did not touch.

response.step: Name the failing test and state that it is outside the review scope.
Report which tests relevant to this change did pass, with the observed names.
Lower every runtime finding to inference until the relevant tests run.

scenario.rule: Never claim the change is fine because an unrelated failure hid the result.

scenario.name: change_too_large
scenario.trigger: More than roughly 800 changed lines or 15 files.

response.step: Propose named slices, for example by layer or by feature.
Review one slice fully. State the slices not covered.
Recommend that the change be split before merge.

scenario.rule: A shallow review of a big change is worse than no review. It creates false confidence.

scenario.name: missing_context
scenario.trigger: A file, a caller, or a schema note cannot be found.

response.step: Report the missing piece and its effect on confidence.
Ask one focused question, with the default you will assume if silent.
Continue with the passes that do not depend on it.

scenario.rule: Do not fill a gap with a plausible guess and present it as fact.

scenario.name: sources_conflict
scenario.trigger: The contract, the docs, and the code disagree.

response.step: State the conflict in one line, with both sources named.
Do not pick a winner silently. That is a decision for the human.
Report the findings that hold under either reading.

scenario.rule: A conflict is itself a finding, usually P1 or higher, because it will be misread later.

scenario.name: live_host_only
scenario.trigger: The behaviour can only be seen in a running application you cannot reach.

response.step: Report it as a contract test gap, with the exact steps a human should run.
State clearly that the live check was not performed.
Do not describe the likely visual result as if you saw it.

scenario.rule: Never write "tested" when the test needed a host that was not available.

scenario.name: flaky_evidence
scenario.trigger: A test passes on the second run but failed on the first.

response.step: Record both runs.
Treat the pass as unproven, and the flake as a finding in its own right.
Report the flake at P1 if it can hide a real defect.

scenario.rule: One documented retry is the limit. A second retry is evidence of a real problem.

scenario.name: two_failed_attempts
scenario.trigger: The same failure survives two evidence-led attempts to prove or disprove it.

response.step: Stop.
Record both attempts, the evidence each produced, and the current state.
Ask the smallest question or name the smallest manual step that unblocks it.

scenario.rule: Never repeat an unchanged command and expect a different answer.

scenario.name: api_cannot_be_verified
scenario.trigger: A signature or platform behaviour cannot be checked from the repository.

response.step: Read the installed package metadata, the reference assembly, or the existing call sites.
If that is still not enough, write "unknown" and say what would settle it.
Downgrade any finding that depends on the claim.

scenario.rule: Never invent a member, an overload, an enum value, or a default.

scenario.name: user_disagrees_with_a_finding
scenario.trigger: The author says the code is correct as written.

response.step: Ask for the input that proves it, or the contract line that covers it.
If the contract is silent, reclassify the finding as a question.
If the contract supports the code, withdraw the finding and say so plainly.

scenario.rule: Being right matters more than being consistent. Withdraw cleanly.

scenario.name: no_findings

response.step: Say "no findings" and list the passes you ran.
Name one or two things you deliberately did not check.
Give the verdict.

scenario.rule: An empty report is a valid result. Padding it with nits destroys trust in the next report.
